## Result
Resolved the one bin/spud conflict (member subparsers, ~line 6181-6188): kept SPD-017's `member list` subparser and SPD-013's updated `resum` help text (names the SPD-013 breakdown addition, superseding origin/main's older wording, which is dropped as redundant). Both tickets' behaviour is present.

Consistency check across the merge found and fixed one real gap, and that fix surfaced one stale test:

1. bin/spud: `cmd_member_list`'s --ticket branch called `team_tree(con, t)` without `ctx.pricing`, unlike `cmd_card` (`team_tree(con, t, pricing)`). Since `team_tree`'s only two callers are `cmd_card` and `cmd_member_list`, this meant `member list --ticket` would report every member as unpriced even when a real price table exists, contradicting its own docstring ("what card's team shows for one ticket"). Fixed by passing `ctx.pricing`, matching cmd_card.

2. tests/test_members.py: that fix (and, independently, SPD-013's change to team_tree itself) breaks SPD-017's `test_json_shape_matches_member_show`, which asserted `member list`'s per-member dict is byte-for-byte equal to `member show`'s. SPD-013's `team_tree` now always adds `tokens`/`cost_usd`/`not_priced` to every node it returns (card's team, and so member list's --ticket form); `member show` returns a plain `member_dict` that never carries them. This is a genuine disagreement between the two tickets' expectations on the merged tree, not something either ticket got wrong on its own. Updated the test to assert the extra keys are exactly `{tokens, cost_usd, not_priced}` and that every other field still matches member show, rather than requiring full equality.

Checked and found consistent, no change needed: `get_member`/`cmd_member_resum`'s ref handling (line ~3753) already calls `get_member(con, ref)` with the default `allow_handle=True`, so it inherits SPD-017's handle-accepting behaviour automatically. `flatten_team`, `card_total_line`, `team_totals`, `cmd_card` needed no changes. Only two call sites of `team_tree` exist in the file (card, list); `render_ticket`/`render_targets` (the note renderer) already pass `ctx.pricing` correctly and were untouched by the conflict.
